rv.q: This spellbinding West End production was well worth the wait.
This is one of the best West End musicals around.
With so many exceptional voices whirling around them, Orpheus and Eurydice risk becoming supporting players at times, but their final, ill-starred journey still touches the heart.
But it washes over you like a steam bath.
The writer-composer's score is catchy and eclectic but often bombastic, her lyrics pretentious or nonsensical. The book turns a 20-minute story into a meandering, confused two hours.
Lay aside all unhelpful preconceptions of Greek myth and musical theatre and allow yourself to be wooed by the hazy, dazy atmosphere of this splendidly sultry show.
This spellbinding West End production was well worth the wait.
It’s a terrific musical and a sensational evening but in the end, for me, the material just doesn’t quite coalesce into the ending I long for.
And that, in the end, is the point of the show: the old song these artists sing may be a sad one, but at its core is the hope that in some future retelling we might change the narrative.

But there is a dramatic artlessness that verges on the naive, a lack of shape and intent; however scorching the singing, this is an undernourished parade of numbers rather an achieved theatrical work.
there’s no getting away from the fact that Hadestown is barely more than a concert performance of the album
